job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: The evolution of print technology is often misunderstood as a sudden invention. While Johannes Gutenberg is famous for developing the mechanical printing press in Europe around 1448, he was not the first to use movable type; woodblock printing and early metal type systems had existed in East Asia for centuries. When print technology arrived in India, its impact was gradual rather than instantaneous. Colonial authorities viewed the growing influence of vernacular newspapers with suspicion, leading to the Vernacular Press Act of 1878. This law did not ban all newspapers; instead, it empowered the government to censor reports and editorials that were deemed seditious. Furthermore, the spread of print did not instantly transform society. For instance, while print culture provided reading materials for women, it did not make all Indian women literate overnight. Literacy rates improved slowly as social reformers and families began to encourage girls' education over several decades. The print revolution was a complex process of technological adaptation and social change, shaped by both colonial restrictions and the persistent efforts of local communities to expand access to knowledge.

items.evidence: While Johannes Gutenberg is famous for developing the mechanical printing press in Europe around 1448, he was not the first to use movable type; woodblock printing and early metal type systems had existed in East Asia for centuries.
items.q: A student says Gutenberg invented printing from nothing. Which fact shows this is wrong?
options: Printing methods already existed in East Asia earlier
Printing began in Europe and then reached China
His press was too slow to copy books
Printing was only known in Europe around 1448
items.explain: Woodblock and early metal type had existed in East Asia for centuries before Gutenberg's press.

wrong.why: thinks printing started in Europe and spread to China
assumes the press was fast and cheap from the start
thinks Gutenberg was first to use movable type

items.evidence: This law did not ban all newspapers; instead, it empowered the government to censor reports and editorials that were deemed seditious.
items.q: An Indian editor in 1878 prints a report the government finds seditious. What may happen?
options: The government may censor the report
The government shuts every newspaper in India
The editor is allowed to print freely
The report is left alone by the law
items.explain: The Vernacular Press Act let the government censor seditious reports, but it did not ban all newspapers.

wrong.why: thinks the Act banned all newspapers
thinks the press was always free of control
thinks the law did not touch seditious reports

items.evidence: Colonial authorities viewed the growing influence of vernacular newspapers with suspicion, leading to the Vernacular Press Act of 1878.
items.q: Why did the British bring in the Vernacular Press Act of 1878?
options: They distrusted the rising power of Indian newspapers
They wanted to help newspapers grow faster
They found newspapers were too costly to print
They wished to end all printing in India
items.explain: The authorities viewed the growing influence of vernacular newspapers with suspicion, so they passed the Act.

wrong.why: thinks the government supported a free press
invents a cost reason not in the passage
thinks the aim was to ban all printing

items.evidence: Literacy rates improved slowly as social reformers and families began to encourage girls' education over several decades.
items.q: How did women's literacy in India grow after print reached the country?
options: Slowly, as reformers and families backed girls' schooling
Quickly, once books were printed for women
Slowly, as the government ran schools for girls
Quickly, because print made reading easy for all
items.explain: Literacy improved slowly over decades as reformers and families encouraged girls' education, not overnight.

wrong.why: thinks print made women literate immediately
credits the government, which the passage does not say
thinks print gave everyone easy access to reading
